1.explanation: This minimal React app mounts the Carbon MultiSelect with two items pre-selected (`initialSelectedItems`). No custom labels are provided for the built-in “×” clear button, so under IBM’s DAP vJuly 2019 rules you will see an error “An interactive element/widget must have an accessible name.” Expanding the menu exposes each option as a checkbox input with identical group names but no `<fieldset>` or ARIA group, triggering the grouping-roles violation. Clearing and re-opening shows the same grouping errors minus one (since two items are removed). You can run the DAP extension in Chrome on this page to reproduce all three screenshots.
1.bug_scenario: The user is rendering the Carbon React MultiSelect component with pre-selected items and then running IBM’s DAP (Accessibility Checker). In the first screenshot you can see that the little “×” clear-all button (rendered as a `<div role="button">` with an SVG inside) has no accessible name or label. When the menu is expanded (second screenshot), DAP reports seven violations under “Use grouping roles or elements to identify related form controls” — i.e. each checkbox option in the listbox has the same `name` but they are not wrapped in a `<fieldset>`/`<legend>` or a group role. After clicking the “×” to clear the selections and re-expanding the menu (third screenshot), six grouping-role violations remain. All of these can be reproduced with the default MultiSelect usage having `initialSelectedItems` set.
